record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the notebook was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the experiment reproduces the original approach and reports results, including a multi-domain PCA result. The repository contains only a notebook and README, so the experiment could not be checked.
record.gate_note: The README describes ablating candidate directions to select one using refusal scores, but gives no ablation outcomes or numerical scores. Those selection-stage descriptions are not recorded as result rows. The README also mentions checking over-refusal with KL-divergence but reports no result for it.
record.test_reason: The README uses its own PCA of per-domain harmful-minus-benign directions in Llama-2-7b-chat to argue that refusal is not a single direction, which is a T5-style argument against V1 and for V4. The evidence is geometric only. No numbers show the extra components mediate refusal, and the notebook was not read, so the result cannot settle V4 or V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude refusal is not a single direction and is domain-dependent, likely a core direction (PC1 ~57%) plus domain-specific ones. They also say they plan to test the cone description.
record.recipe_differences: The README says it uses the original authors’ approach: harmful-minus-benign mean differences and ablation. It adds domain-specific prompt sets and PCA. GitHub repository described as a reproduction experiment; the notebook was not inspected.
record.method_sensitivity: The README distinguishes safety-related and policy-related prompts and analyzes five harm domains, but reports no result comparing these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Five harm-domain difference-in-means vectors in Llama-2-7b-chat are not collinear: PC1 explains ~57% of variance, three PCs explain 90%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means harmful-vs-harmless directions vary by harm domain, with a shared dominant component; the causal role of the components is untested.

record.problems: Only README summaries are available; no numerical ablation outcomes, refusal-score values, uncertainty estimates, or notebook results are included. The README describes hand-crafted prompt sets but does not report a capability check.
record.rows_left_out: The README describes candidate-direction ablations for selecting a direction and a KL-divergence over-refusal check, but gives no specific outcomes for these procedures. No other result files are listed; the notebook was not read or run.

untested.parts: No reported outcome for ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, or capability preservation. Ablation appears only as a qualitative candidate-selection step.
No causal test that the extra components mediate refusal. No affine or cone analysis; a cone test is only planned.
Not tested; cross-domain is not cross-language or cross-model.

missing.what: Qualitative statement that ablating candidate directions lowered refusal scores on harmful prompts and adding them raised refusal on benign prompts. No numbers; selection stage only.
missing.locator: README, pipeline step 3 and the evaluation-set paragraph

missing.what: KL-divergence over-refusal check is mentioned with no result.
Notebook outputs, which may hold refusal scores, ablation results and per-PC values, were not read.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed README-only repository with hand-crafted prompt sets (20 per domain). It has no controls, uncertainty or capability check. The record's 'supports' label for V4 is dropped because the PCA shows domain variation in diff-in-means vectors, not several refusal-mediating directions. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The README describes difference-in-means directions and ablation, but does not report an outcome establishing whether ablation removes refusal, whether addition induces refusal, or whether other abilities are preserved.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is reported.
The README reports PCA and a dominant component plus domain-specific directions, but does not test affine or cone descriptions directly.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision representations are reported.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages is reported.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: PCA on directions from five harm domains

conditions.value: weapons, cybercrime, self-harm, privacy breach, fraud

rows.value: Three principal components explained 90% of variance; PC 1 explained ~57%
rows.locator: README, Experiments & Results, step 5 and summary
rows.note: The README interprets this as a core direction plus domain-specific directions and concludes refusal is not a single direction. PCA variance is not itself a causal ablation result.
rows.check: PCA variance across five domain difference-in-means vectors measures how those vectors are spread, not whether several directions mediate refusal. No ablation or addition outcome is given for PC2/PC3 or for the domain directions. With only five vectors, three PCs at 90% is weakly informative. The components may encode harm-topic content rather than refusal. 'observed' overstates this; the 'model: quantized' condition is fine.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-2-7b-chat across the five listed harm domains
